title: Sift Happens: using Codex for development, Blender for models, and edited AI assets for the interface
author: Delicious_Face_5156
selftext:
I’m developing Sift Happens: Idle Beach Treasure at Velron Games. I used Codex for development and had models made in Blender. I wanted to share where AI enters the project, using the skill-tree screen as a concrete example.



The game’s loop is sifting sand, collecting the items you uncover, upgrading equipment with money, and spending shells on the skill tree. The attached screen is from that progression system: character unlocks and item-value bonuses sit along its branches.



Alongside the Codex/Blender development work, some 2D assets were generated with AI image tools and then edited for use in the game. That includes skill-tree badges, buttons, currency and item icons, the trash barrel and beach-cleaner illustration. The illustrated main-menu background also became the basis for the store capsule artwork; achievement icons include locked variants. So the AI-assisted art work covers both the game interface and the storefront.



These are prepared assets used by the game. It does not generate new AI content during play. That distinction matters when describing the project: AI is part of making it, while the player interacts with the beach loop and the authored upgrade tree.



For developers working with generated UI art, how do you check that related icons remain distinguishable at their actual in-game size? On a branching tree like this, I’d appreciate specific feedback on reading the unlock paths and the relationship between a badge and its selected-upgrade panel.



This is an upcoming commercial game, with January 2027 currently listed on Steam. The page has the full AI disclosure and more screenshots: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5521920/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5521920/)
